introduction.definition: A pulse-jet baghouse filters dust from gas through rows of fabric bags supported on wire cages. Dust builds a cake on the outside of the bags; short reverse pulses of compressed air flex the bags row by row so the cake falls into the hopper, from where a rotary airlock discharges it.

pressure.title: Filter on the outside, clean by a pulse
pressure.description: Dirty gas flows from outside to inside through the bags; dust builds a cake that itself becomes the fine filter (outlet dust often < 5–10 mg/Nm³). As the cake grows the pressure drop rises (typically held ≈ 1–1.5 kPa); the controller then fires a short compressed-air pulse down each row in turn, flexing the bags so the cake drops to the hopper. Air-to-cloth ratio (≈ 0.8–1.5 m/min for pulse-jet) sets the bag area. Watch temperature (bag limits), dew point (wet cake) and spark ignition risk.

video_tutorials.title: Baghouse Dust Collector — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Baghouse Dust Collector.
A pulse-jet baghouse filters dust from gas through rows of fabric bags supported on wire cages.
Dust builds a cake on the outside of the bags; short reverse pulses of compressed air flex the bags row by row so the cake falls into the hopper, from where a rotary airlock discharges it.
Typical applications include cement, mining, alumina and power plants; dust extraction, kilns and dry-scrubber product collection.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Casing (dirty-gas chamber), Pyramid Hopper & Clean-Air Plenum, Airlock Rotor.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Baghouse Dust Collector — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Baghouse Dust Collector.
Check ΔP and opacity / dust monitor.
Check pulse valves and compressed air.
Replace bags (≈ 2–5 years).
Watch for bag leak: dust emission spike. Common cause: abrasion, burn holes.
Watch for high δp: reduced airflow. Common cause: blinding (moisture), cleaning failure.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
